data.title: Revvity slips as CFRA downgrades on limited near-term upside
data.description:
Revvity shares fell on Friday following a five-day winning streak as CFRA downgraded the life sciences company to Hold from Buy, citing a less attractive upside opportunity in the near term after its recent rally.

“Though we think RVTY’s fundamental story remains compelling, we think near-term upside is less attractive following recent valuation expansion,” analyst Daniel Rich wrote, according to Bloomberg.

The Waltham, Massachusetts-based company, formerly known as PerkinElmer, has added nearly 50% in value this year, with the stock trading near a post-pandemic high. The downgrade came after its shares set a new 52-week high earlier this week after the company presented at Baird’s 2026 Global Healthcare Conference.

“We look to 3Q results to help confirm indications of instrument backlog conversion and software sales momentum, which we think could lead to stronger earnings guidance that helps normalize RVTY’s valuation," Rich added as he boosted his price target to $157 from $145 per share.

data.title: Netflix just got a warning that could change the growth story
data.description:
Netflix Inc. (NFLX, Financials), the streaming company expanding into sports, gaming and advertising, is facing a new concern from Wall Street: people may simply be watching less.

Wells Fargo downgraded Netflix to Underweight from Equal Weight and cut its price target to $57 from $80.

Shares fell about 3.5% in premarket trading Friday. The bank's concern goes deeper than the stock price.

Netflix viewership fell 8% year over year during the first half of 2026, according to Wells Fargo. Hours watched among its Top 100 original programs declined 3%.

The firm expects another pressure point in the second half, forecasting a more than 20% year-over-year decline in Netflix's Top 100 originals.

Netflix has been trying to widen its reach through sports, gaming, documentaries and content distributed more directly through YouTube.

But Wells Fargo sees a risk that the company is missing the kind of original shows that become cultural events and keep subscribers watching.

That could become expensive to fix. The firm sees the possibility of another content-spending push, while also lowering its expectations for future operating margins.

Netflix has spent years proving it can turn streaming scale into profits. Investors now have another question to watch: whether it can keep people watching without pushing content costs sharply higher.

data.title: Stocks Fall as Treasury Yields Rise — WSJ
data.description:
By Caitlin McCabe

Friday closes a chapter in investing history, with Warren Buffett stepping down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway. In the post-Buffett era, attention is turning back to bond yields.

Global government bond yields are on the upswing, after pausing their rally earlier Friday. The 10-year Treasury yield just hit 5% again.

The move higher in bond yields largely mirrors oil prices, which have erased most of their losses from earlier today. Brent is trading around $105 a barrel. The U.K. Maritime Trade Operations Centre, which is affiliated with Britain's navy, reported Friday that a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was struck on Wednesday.

For now, higher bond yields are dampening stock indexes, which are all in the red. Also weighing on sentiment: data from the Federal Reserve showing that manufacturing output fell 0.3% in August following seven straight months of gains.

The AI trade is still working, though, with shares of hyperscalers, chip makers and data-storage providers climbing.

Meanwhile, the Bank of Japan raised its benchmark interest rate, as expected, to its highest level since 1995. Even so, dissent from two board members triggered a drop in the yen by raising doubts about the pace of further policy changes.

Write to Caitlin McCabe at caitlin.mccabe@wsj.com

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Allied Gold Advances Ethiopia Mine Toward Startup as First Ore Enters Circuit
data.description:
By Adriano Marchese

Allied Gold shares rose Friday after it said it has connected its mine in Ethiopia to the power grid and processed its first ore, marking a major milestone as the project comes online.

Shares traded 4.9% higher at 31.55 Canadian dollars ($22.55).

The miner late Thursday said that it has connected the Kurmuk mine to the national electrical grid, and the first ore has been fed through its processing facilities. The progress transitions Kurmuk from a development-stage asset into a significant growth operation, which the company calls one of its premier gold mines.

The company noted that it continues to mine the deposit as planned, with ore stockpiles building to support the ramp-up to commercial production.

Currently, the company is sitting on a stockpile of about 1 million metric tons, with plans to increase it to 1.5 million tons before it begins to feed its processing circuit at full capacity.

Allied expects to pour its first gold soon, it said, as downstream circuits come online.

data.title: Global shares fall, Treasury yields rise as central banks double down on inflation fight
data.description:
Key points:
  • BOJ hike lifts rates to 1.25%, highest level in 31 years
  • Dollar rises against yen after two BOJ board members dissent
  • Brent crude falls, gold gains

By Amanda Cooper and Chibuike Oguh

Equities around the world fell while Treasury yields rose on Friday, as markets approached the end of a turbulent week marked by a global push by central banks to quell inflation.

On Wall Street, the three main indexes were lower, with materials, utilities and real estate stocks leading declines. The benchmark S&P 500 and the Dow were on track for weekly losses, while the Nasdaq was set to post a weekly gain.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.4%, the S&P 500 fell 0.2%, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.1%.

Stocks in Europe fell 1.1% and were headed for a weekly loss. MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe EURONEXT:IACWI fell 0.2%.

Monetary policy has been the prime focus this week, as the war in the Middle East nears the seven-month mark with few signs of ending, which is keeping oil prices above $100 per barrel and fanning inflation fears. That has also led to a rise in yields across major government bond markets.

"The market is coming to the realization of a higher interest-rate environment on a go-forward basis," said Kieran Osborne, chief investment officer at Mission Wealth.

"The Fed clearly indicated that they're likely to raise rates one more time and then central banks globally are sort of on the path to try to rein in inflation. The situation in the Middle East doesn't appear to be abating anytime soon."

CENTRAL BANK MOVES

The yen weakened and Japanese government bonds fell after the Bank of Japan raised rates to a 31-year high of 1.25%. The decision, though expected, excited yen bears with two board members dissenting to the hike.

The Japanese yen weakened 0.6% against the greenback to 156.88 per dollar. The Japanese currency has risen 1.8% so far this month, driven by expectations of a faster pace of hikes from the BOJ and early signs of repatriation from Japanese investors.

The BOJ decision wraps up the series of major central bank meetings in which policymakers have ratcheted up hawkish rhetoric.

The Federal Reserve raised rates for the first time in three years on Wednesday and switched to a more aggressive stance on inflation, which knocked the yen, putting it on course for its worst weekly performance against the dollar in two years, down 2.6%.

The Bank of England on Thursday left UK rates unchanged but said it may have to hike if the Iran war drags on. The European Central Bank last week also flagged the need for further tightening as it raised rates. And Australia's top central banker on Friday said some of the upside risks to inflation flagged by policymakers appeared to be materialising.

The euro fell 0.1% at $1.1465.

The dollar index , which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, rose 0.1%.

OIL PRICES RETREAT

Brent crude futures fell 0.1% to $104.67 following a Reuters report that China has asked Tehran to help rein in the Houthis after their military blitz over the past week. That, together with hopes Gulf exporters may find alternative routes to ship oil, put crude futures on course for a weekly decline.

Bond yields edged up after another brutal selloff this week that took the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield beyond 5% to its highest since 2007. It was last up 5.32 basis points at 4.947%.

Yields across the euro zone (DE10YT=RR) and in Britain (GB10YT=RR) have also hit multi-year highs in the last week, but by Friday were only a touch higher.

Spot gold rose 0.3% to $4,352.77 an ounce.

data.title: Evercore Resets Apple Stock Price Target for 2026
data.description:
Apple could have more room to run despite trading near record highs, with Evercore ISI raising its price target to $380 and maintaining an Outperform rating after its latest consumer survey pointed to a stronger-than-expected iPhone 18 upgrade cycle.

Apple shares were recently trading around $337, putting Evercore's new target roughly 13% above current levels. The stock has already surged about 35% over the past six months and sits close to its 52-week high of $344.57.

Evercore's annual survey of nearly 4,000 consumers showed particularly strong interest in Apple's premium devices.

About 53% of respondents planning an iPhone purchase said they expect to buy an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max, above the 51% historical average. Interest in the Pro Max alone rose to 32% from 29% last year.

That mix matters because higher-priced models can lift average selling prices and support margins even if overall unit growth remains modest.

Replacement demand also appears healthy.

About 67% of respondents said an aging phone was driving their decision to upgrade, sharply above 48% last year.

Evercore also saw encouraging demand beyond the iPhone. Apple Watch purchase intentions increased to 38% from 34%, while AirPods intentions climbed to 43% from 40%.

Investors Takeaway

The biggest positive is not simply stronger iPhone demand, but the premium mix.

If more buyers gravitate toward Pro and Pro Max models, Apple could generate stronger revenue per device while supporting its already powerful ecosystem economics.

The upcoming iPhone Duo may provide another catalyst. About 14% of survey respondents expressed purchase interest versus 9% for last year's iPhone Air, with Evercore expecting demand could strengthen after consumers see the product following its mid-October launch.

Investors should nevertheless keep valuation in focus.

Apple is already near record territory after a substantial rally, meaning stronger demand may be increasingly reflected in the share price.

The next test is whether robust upgrade intentions convert into actual shipments, higher average selling prices and earnings growth strong enough to justify Evercore's $380 target.

data.title: The Week in Oil: Saudi Oil Exports Under Spotlight
data.description:
By Giulia Petroni

Here's a look at what happened in oil markets in the week of Sept. 14-18 and what the focus will be in the days to come.

OVERVIEW: Oil prices were mixed in afternoon European trading as traders evaluate Saudi supply risks and widening risks from the Middle East war. Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, is trading above $104 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate futures are at around $102 a barrel.

MACRO: Markets are pricing in a more hawkish Federal Reserve after the U.S. central bank raised interest rates at this week's meeting for the first time in three years, while signaling that another hike could follow. The shift comes as the Fed's progress on inflation has stalled, with the war in Iran driving up oil and broader energy prices, threatening to reignite inflationary pressures and complicate the path toward lower rates.

GEOPOLITICAL RISKS: Global oil flows through key shipping routes in the Middle East risk remaining disrupted well into 2027, according to analysts, keeping the geopolitical risk premium high.

Saudi Arabia shut down the East-West Pipeline, which connects the Persian Gulf with the Red Sea, prompting a sharp rise in oil prices at the start of the week. Prices subsequently fell amid expectations that the kingdom could soon restore some flows through the damaged pipeline. However, Saudi Arabia has not provided a timeline for restarting the pipeline, with its energy ministry stating that technical teams are assessing its integrity following attacks on energy infrastructure.

Meanwhile, the security situation across the region remains volatile as Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen have also expanded their territorial control.

SUPPLY AND DEMAND: On the supply side, the disruption to Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline and lower oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz are creating concerns about reduced global crude supplies. Saudi Arabia's temporary shutdown of the pipeline could potentially remove around 3.5 million-4 million barrels per day from exports if the outage continues, according to Kpler estimates. Meanwhile, the seven-day average of flows through the Strait of Hormuz stood at 10.0 million barrels per day, well below the pre-war level of 17.1 million barrels per day, the firm said. The continued shortfall and large daily swings indicate that oil shipments through the Strait remain disrupted, keeping pressure on global crude supply and increasing uncertainty in the oil market.

WHAT'S NEXT: Looking ahead, developments in the Middle East, particularly around the East-West Pipeline, are likely to remain a key focus for oil markets. Market participants remain cautious about how quickly Saudi Arabia can restore operations, given that the kingdom has not yet provided a firm timeline for the pipeline's restart. Until there is greater clarity, oil prices are likely to remain elevated as inventories at Yanbu, the Red Sea export terminal and endpoint of the East-West Pipeline, continue to be drawn down.

Beyond geopolitical developments, attention will also turn to the economic calendar, with upcoming PMI data, initial jobless claims and consumer sentiment surveys providing further insight into the health of the global economy and potentially influencing expectations for energy demand and broader market conditions.

data.title: Inflation Running Too Hot Even Without Oil, Fed's Schmid Says
data.description:
By Dean Seal

The economy's inflation problem is being driven by more than just high oil prices, Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid said.

Schmid reiterated points he has made all summer about inflation running too hot even when excluding energy prices, sparking the need for fiscal tightening. He spoke at the Independent Community Bankers of Colorado Annual Convention on Friday.

"A broad range of goods and services are showing price growth inconsistent with our price stability target," Schmid said.

Schmid's comments are among the first from a Federal Reserve official since the Federal Open Market Committee voted unanimously on Wednesday to raise interest rates for the first time in three years.

While Schmid isn't a voting member on the committee this year, he said he supported the rate hike, calling it a step in the right direction. Inflation has run above the Fed's 2% target for more than five years, and the most recent readings suggest the pace is still trending above 3%, Schmid said.

Because the rest of the economy is performing well, with a balanced labor market, persistent consumer spending and strong business investment, inflation is Schmid's primary concern, he added.

data.title: California to Reconsider AI 'Kill Switch' With Newsom's New Executive Order — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Anita Hamilton

California Gov. Gavin Newsom issued an executive order Friday aimed at strengthening the state's artificial-intelligence safety and security laws, prompted by recent alarm bells about the technology's threats to human safety.

The order calls for the implementation of both third-party oversight as well as independent audits. As part of the order, experts will consider a proposal that would require AI companies to develop a so-called "kill switch"-an emergency shut-off feature-for so-called frontier models.

OpenAI, Anthropic, and Alphabet's Google, all of which are based in California, didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

data.title: Goldman Sachs Delivers Surprising Verdict on Big Tech Stocks
data.description:
Wall Street's biggest technology stocks are losing one of the defining characteristics of the past several years: their hefty valuation premium over the rest of the S&P 500.

Goldman Sachs Research says the forward price-to-earnings multiples of the market's largest companies have fallen sharply and are now converging toward the valuation of the other 495 stocks in the S&P 500.

The shift is notable because mega-cap technology companies historically commanded much richer multiples, reflecting faster growth, dominant competitive positions and enormous free-cash-flow generation.

That gap is now narrowing.

Goldman points to two major pressures: a higher cost of capital and dramatically greater capital intensity.

Companies including Microsoft , Amazon , Meta Platforms and Alphabet are committing enormous sums to artificial-intelligence infrastructure, including data centers, chips and power capacity.

Those investments may support substantial future growth, but they also consume cash today.

At the same time, higher borrowing costs reduce the present value investors assign to future earnings and cash flows.

The result has been a significant valuation de-rating among Wall Street's largest companies.

Investors Takeaway

The narrowing valuation gap creates an unusual setup.

Mega-cap technology stocks may no longer carry the valuation premium investors often associate with them, even though many still have superior growth profiles and exposure to the AI infrastructure boom.

That could strengthen the bull case if AI spending begins producing faster revenue and earnings growth.

But the cheaper relative valuation also reflects a legitimate concern: these businesses are becoming substantially more capital intensive.

Investors should therefore focus less on headline AI spending and more on the returns generated from that spending.

If Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Alphabet can convert massive infrastructure investments into sustained earnings growth, today's lower relative multiples could eventually look attractive.

If returns on AI capital disappoint, however, the disappearance of the valuation premium may prove justified rather than an opportunity.

The key takeaway from Goldman is that mega-cap tech is no longer priced as dramatically different from the rest of the market. Now the companies have to prove their growth deserves to be.

data.title: Nebius Offers Fresh Clue About AI's Spending Boom
data.description:
Nebius Group shares jumped nearly 9% in Thursday premarket trading after the AI cloud provider reportedly raised prices across several compute services, offering a potentially important signal that demand for scarce GPU capacity remains strong.

According to a customer communication circulated online, Nebius plans to increase prices for several on-demand GPU offerings beginning October 1.

The changes reportedly cover Nvidia's H100, H200, B200 and B300 accelerators, some of the most important chips used for artificial-intelligence training and inference workloads.

Nebius has not publicly confirmed the pricing changes and did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The reported increases extend beyond GPUs.

Prices for AMD EPYC Genoa CPU compute are expected to rise 25% to $0.015 per vCPU-hour from $0.012, while memory pricing tied to Genoa systems is reportedly increasing about 41% to $0.0045 per GiB-hour from $0.0032.

The market reaction spread beyond Nebius.

IREN shares rose about 5.1% in premarket trading, while CoreWeave gained roughly 6.1%, suggesting investors interpreted the reported increases as a positive read-through for the wider neocloud industry.

Investors Takeaway

The bigger issue is pricing power.

Neocloud companies are spending heavily to secure Nvidia GPUs, build data centers and expand power capacity. Their investment cases become much stronger if demand remains tight enough to support higher rental rates.

Reported price increases across both newer and older GPU generations could suggest customers are still competing for available AI compute rather than waiting for cheaper capacity.

That would support margins and improve the economics of future infrastructure spending.

The risk is that the information has not yet been formally confirmed by Nebius.

Investors should watch whether the company verifies the changes, how customers respond and whether competitors follow with similar pricing moves.

If higher prices stick without hurting utilization, the signal would be bullish not just for Nebius but for CoreWeave, IREN and other AI infrastructure providers.

The key question is whether this represents durable pricing power or simply a temporary response to tight supply.

data.title: Brazil police seize devices from former iFood employee in trade secrets probe
data.description:
Key points:
  • Former iFood strategic sales executive probed, police inspector says
  • Escalating rivalry after Keeta and DiDi-backed 99Food entered Brazil
  • iFood holds roughly 80% of domestic food-delivery market

By Marcela Ayres

Brazilian police carried out a search-and-seizure operation this week against a former iFood employee suspected of downloading confidential commercial information before leaving the food-delivery company to join rival 99Food, according to the lead investigator.

The case marks the latest development in a broader probe into alleged corporate espionage in Brazil's multibillion-dollar delivery industry, where competition has intensified following the entry of Chinese-backed platforms Keeta, owned by Meituan , and 99Food, controlled by ride-hailing firm DiDi Global .

The police operation carried out on Wednesday targeted a former strategic sales executive who had access to sensitive client information, such as sales volumes and customer profiles, while working at iFood, Angelo Lages, the police inspector leading the investigation in Rio de Janeiro, told Reuters.

"The purpose of the search was to collect electronic devices so we can conduct forensic analysis and determine what happened to the data," he said late on Thursday.

99Food said it takes such reports seriously, does not tolerate the use of data obtained through illegal means, and that the individual targeted by the operation is not part of its workforce.

ALLEGED THEFT OF INFORMATION

iFood, owned by Dutch investment group Prosus , controls about 80% of the market, which overall processed about $20 billion in orders last year, according to industry group Abrasel.

In recent months, iFood has publicly alleged attempts to obtain confidential business information through former employees and paid consultations arranged by third-party firms, charges rivals deny.

iFood said this week's operation resulted from a complaint it filed involving the alleged theft of strategic and confidential commercial information by a former employee, adding that it is also pursuing legal measures to protect its data and business partners.

The former employee resigned from iFood in 2025 after informing the company he would join 99Food, the inspector Lages said, adding that an internal review later identified downloads of strategic files shortly before his departure.

The former employee told officers he no longer worked for 99Food and was currently operating as an independent consultant, Lages said. Investigators are also seeking to determine whether other individuals or companies gained access to the information.

ANTITRUST DISPUTES

The allegations of corporate espionage are unfolding alongside a series of ongoing competition disputes before Brazil's antitrust regulator Cade.

Keeta has accused 99Food of using exclusivity clauses and contractual provisions that allegedly make it harder for restaurants to operate across multiple platforms.

Separately, iFood earlier this year asked Cade to scrutinize the expansion strategies of Keeta and 99Food, alleging they rely on heavy subsidies and sustained losses to gain market share.

($1 = 5.1326 reais)

data.title: Nymex Overview: Petroleum Futures See Mixed Action, Remain on Track for Weekly Gains — OPIS
data.description:
Crude oil futures prices were seeing small movement and refined product prices were mixed Friday morning while contracts were set to end the week with gains.

Brent crude futures were seeing small declines heading into Friday afternoon, with the November contract falling by 24cts to $104.64/bbl while December prices were off by 1ct to $99.92/bbl in more active trade at about 11:15 a.m. ET.

If the declines hold, it will mark the third-straight day that Brent prices have weakened.

West Texas Intermediate crude futures were mixed, with the lightly traded October contract rising by 43cts to $102.34/bbl while November prices fell by 17cts to $97.06/bbl.

RBOB futures were also pulling back in early trade, with October prices off by 0.8ct to $3.4993/gal while November prices were trading 1.08cts lower to $3.2378/gal.

ULSD prices were seeing solid gains after two days of declines, with October prices rising by 1.65cts to $5.1304/gal while November prices were 1.32cts higher to $4.9022/gal.

Petroleum prices have been falling in the last few days as worries eased about oil supply from Saudi Arabia, with reports that the kingdom could restore some flows through its damaged East-West Pipeline while also using other work-arounds to meet customer demand despite attempts by Iranian-backed Houthis in Yemen to disrupt oil shipments through the Red Sea.

Still, on Friday news reports indicated that Saudi officials have informed some European refiners they will receive no oil next month due to the pipeline damage.

"Diplomatic signals have added to the downward pressure. Beijing has privately encouraged Tehran to help contain the escalation, while the prospect of contact between Gulf states, Washington and Tehran at the UN General Assembly represents the first visible negotiating channel in months," said Daniel Takieddine, CEO of Sky Links Capital Group.

Retail prices for gasoline and diesel, however, continue to rise, with the national average price for regular unleaded gasoline up 3cts overnight to $4.4687/gal, according to OPIS/AAA data. The average retail diesel price rose more than 5cts to $6.4476/gal.

data.title: Hugoton Royalty Trust: No September 2026 Cash Distribution; Liquidity Doubt Raised
data.description:
Hugoton Royalty Trust announced there will be no cash distribution for September 2026 due to excess cost positions on all three conveyances and a $4,000 reduction in its cash reserve for expenses. The Trustee reports continued accumulated excess costs across Kansas, Oklahoma and Wyoming conveyances, no distributions since July 2023, curtailed spending and substantial doubt about the Trust’s ability to continue as a going concern. The Trustee is reviewing options including possible termination or a sale of the Trust’s net profits interests, while noting financing and a near-term asset sale appear unlikely.

Financial Highlights

  • No cash distribution declared for September 2026; cash reserve decreased by $4,000 for payment of Trust expenses.
  • No unitholder distributions since July 2023 due to accumulated excess costs on the Trust conveyances.
  • Cumulative excess costs (including accrued interest): Kansas $3,408,000 (includes $424,000 interest); Oklahoma $15,154,000 (includes $1,473,000 interest); Wyoming $13,312,000 (includes $1,658,000 interest).
  • Trust received two advance distributions totaling $1,000,000 (net to the Trust) that may be recouped as production costs subject to conditions.

Business Highlights

  • Underlying production volumes attributable to the net overriding royalty for the reported month: gas ~670,000 Mcf and oil ~14,000 barrels (volumes primarily produced in June; recorded when related net profits income is received).
  • Average prices for underlying volumes: gas $2.92 per Mcf and oil $87.91 per barrel for the current month (prior month: gas $2.80/Mcf; oil $100.73/Bbl).
  • Mach Natural Resources reported development costs of $172,000, production expense of $1,769,000 and overhead of $911,000 used in the current month’s royalty calculation.
  • Trustee has deferred discretionary spending, including deferral of the Trustee fee since April 2024, and has engaged third parties to gauge interest in the Trust’s net profits interests though no interest has resulted to date.
  • Trust units were removed from the OTCQB on July 17, 2026 and are trading on the Expert Market on an unsolicited quotes only basis; the Trust is not currently engaging a new independent auditor due to cash constraints and filed a Form 12b-25 on August 14, 2026.

Original SEC Filing: HUGOTON ROYALTY TRUST [ HGTXU ] - 8-K - Sep. 18, 2026

data.title: Jefferies says AI demand remains strong, with Nvidia at the center
data.description:
Key points:
  • Main US indexes modestly red; Dow off most, down ~0.4%
  • Materials weakest S&P 500 sector; just energy up slightly
  • Euro STOXX 600 index down >1%
  • Dollar edges up, gold up ~0.5%, US crude down slightly; bitcoin rallies >5%
  • US 10-year Treasury yield rises to ~5.0%

JEFFERIES SAYS AI DEMAND REMAINS STRONG, WITH NVIDIA AT THE CENTER

Jefferies came away from two days of meetings across the AI supply chain even more bullish on demand, with Nvidia remaining at the center of the story.

According to analysts at the investment bank, in a semiconductor research note dated Thursday, a recurring theme was that concerns about slower AI model releases may be missing the bigger picture. Companies drew a distinction between training the next frontier model and scaling inference for existing ones. AI labs still appear highly focused on deploying and monetizing current models, while new requirements around AI safety and monitoring could create another layer of compute demand.

For Nvidia , the message was clear: demand remains extremely strong. Management said supply is still being allocated, with customer commitments stretching up to three years. Memory, chip-on-wafer-on-substrate (CoWoS) packaging, wafers, substrates and optics remain key bottlenecks, underscoring how tight the market remains. Nvidia also said the data center projects supporting its roughly 70% growth outlook next year have already been vetted, while power availability is becoming less of a constraint.

The company also sounded confident about its competitive position despite growing interest in custom AI chips. Management argued that Nvidia continues to hold a performance edge and noted that about half of revenue comes from customers outside the hyperscalers, where its moat is particularly strong. It also highlighted opportunities around NVLink Fusion and next-generation networking architectures.

Elsewhere, commentary across the ecosystem reinforced the same theme. Broadcom described aggressive demand for leading-edge AI chips, Applied Materials pointed to strong High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) and advanced packaging spending, and optics suppliers highlighted a healthy ramp in 1.6T networking products.

Overall, the meetings suggested AI infrastructure spending remains robust, that demand signals from major AI customers are still aggressive, and that Nvidia remains one of the industry's best-positioned beneficiaries.

data.title: REG - Tata Steel Limited - Disclosure under 30 & 51 SEBI Listing Regulations
data.description:
RNS Number : 4540V Tata Steel Limited 18 September 2026  

Ref: SEC/1069/2026-27

September 18, 2026

London Stock Exchange

London

Dear Madam, Sirs,

Sub: Disclosure under Regulations 30 read with 51 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015

This is further to our disclosures dated April 2, 2024 and May 24, 2024 on the abovementioned subject read with 'material litigation' section of the Board's Report of Tata Steel Limited ('Company') and notes to financial statements, both forming part of the 11th Integrated Report and 118th Annual Accounts of the Company for FY2025-26, in connection with loans obligations of the Company arising from Steel Development Fund ('SDF').

Background:

On April 2, 2024, the Company filed a writ petition before the Hon'ble High Court of Calcutta ('Hon'ble High Court'), in the matter of rejection of a representation made by the Company in respect of waiver of loans availed by the Company from SDF (in parity with SAIL), managed by Joint Plant Committee ('JPC'), Ministry of Steel. The matter was heard by the Hon'ble High Court over several hearings.

On May 24, 2024, the Hon'ble High Court (Single Bench) dismissed the writ petition filed by the Company, with a liberty to the Company to approach the JPC. The Company sought further legal remedies and filed an appeal against this order before the Hon'ble High Court of Calcutta (Division Bench). This appeal is pending before the Hon'ble High Court of Calcutta.

On January 17, 2025, the Company received a demand from the Ministry of Steel to make payment towards outstanding balance of SDF loan. During FY2026, the Company discharged its liability towards JPC aggregating to ₹2,970 crore, without prejudice to its rights and contentions in the appeal.

Present Status:

The Management believed that an interim protection was necessary to safeguard the amounts deposited by the Company with JPC. Accordingly, the Company filed an Interim Application bearing IA no. GA/2/2026 before the Hon'ble High Court of Calcutta seeking injunction on JPC utilizing the said amount of ₹2,970 crore.

The IA NO. GA/2/2026 was heard by the Hon'ble High Court of Calcutta on September 17, 2026.

As per the order of the Hon'ble High Court of Calcutta dated September 17, 2026 received by the Company today i.e. September 18, 2026, Hon'ble High Court has disposed of the interim application with the direction that till the appeal is disposed of, the fund shall not be utilised or disbursed to third parties.

This disclosure is being made by the Company in compliance with Regulations 30 and 51 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended.

This is for your information and records.
